summary: Hironobu Minami works in Buddhist studies. He has held posts as a research assistant at Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism (attested 2015) and associate professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Hiroo Kashiwagi is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo (~1958–1963) and taught Waso Harada. He served as a professor at Mie Chukyo University (attested 1982).

Hiroo Sato specializes in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1973–1982) and held positions at Morioka College (~1982–1990) and Tohoku University (~2001–2019, as professor).

Hiroshi Aoyagi specializes in linguistics, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at International Christian University (~1980–1986) and earned a PhD from the University of Southern California (1991–1998). He became a professor at Nanzan University in 1989.

Hiroshi Araki is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who completed his degrees, including a PhD, at Kyoto University. His academic career includes posts at Aichi Prefectural University, Osaka University, and as professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2010–2025).

Hiroshi Arami works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He has held lecturer posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (both attested 2026).
Hiroshi Deguchi studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1953) and held an academic post at Hokkaido University.
Hiroshi Kanaseki specialized in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1948–1952) and held a post at Tenri University from approximately 1960 to 1997.

Hiroshi Kanno specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Educated at the University of Tokyo (~1972–1984), he served as director at Soka University (1997–2009) and the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology (~2001–2011), and became professor at the International University of Health and Welfare in 2015.

Hiroshi Kuroda is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University (~1974–1976). He served as associate professor at Osaka Gakuin University (attested 1983–1990) and Osaka Gakuin Junior College (attested 1988).

Hiroshi Marui is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and under Albrecht Wezler. He served as associate professor at the University of Tokyo (1992, 1995, 1999–2018) and taught Kei Kataoka and Hisataka Ishida.
Hiroshi Maruyama works in Indology. In 1987, he was attested as a professor at Osaka University and head of the Ayurveda Research Society.
Hiroshi Nemoto specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed an MA at Hiroshima University, where he later served as a professor (attested 2015–2016 and 2026).
Hiroshi Tokushige works in Buddhist studies. He has held appointments at Koyasan University as a commissioned researcher (attested 2015) and as a special-appointment lecturer (attested 2026).
Hiroshi Yamashita is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied abroad at the University of Madras. He served as an associate professor at Tohoku University (attested 1996–1999).

Hirotaka Kato is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a research assistant at the Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism (attested 2015) and as an associate professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).
Hirotomo Teranishi served as a director at Soka University (attested 2010–2012), having succeeded Hiroshi Kanno in 2009.
Hiroyuki Kato was a scholar of philosophy and other fields. He held positions at Bansho Shirabesho (~1860–1862), Kaisei School (~1869–1877), and the University of Tokyo (~1877–1893).
Hisanosuke Izui was a linguist who studied at Kyoto University from around 1927 to 1930. He later held an academic post at Kyoto Sangyo University (~1969–1980).

Hisao Inagaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Kobe City University of Foreign Studies, Ryukoku University, and the University of London. He taught at SOAS (1969–1981) and served as professor at Ryukoku University (1981–1998).
